central_node: Water as a Finite Shared Resource and Ecosystem Foundation

key_details: Total global water represented by 200 ml glass
Usable freshwater equals only ~5 ml (1 teaspoon or 2.5%)
97.5% of Earth's water is salty ocean water
real_world_examples: Proportional glass demonstration (200 ml vs 5 ml)

key_details: Surface water in rivers, streams, lakes, ponds
Underground aquifers stored beneath soil layers
Glaciers and polar ice caps holding frozen freshwater
Rainwater seeps through loose unpaved soil into aquifers
Tree roots loosen soil structure and slow surface runoff
Soak pits and green lawns promote natural recharge
real_world_examples: Rainwater harvesting soak pits in homes and schools

key_details: Impervious concrete roads block water infiltration
Paved surfaces force rainwater into storm drains
Excessive tubewell pumping depletes underground water tables
real_world_examples: Concrete pavements in rapidly expanding cities

key_details: Waxy leaf coating repels water droplets and prevents rotting
Air spaces in stems enable floating
Flexible submerged stems bend with water currents
real_world_examples: Lotus and water lily floating leaves

key_details: Long thin legs allow wading without disturbing prey
Pincers catch prey and tail breathing tubes extract air underwater
real_world_examples: Pond herons standing in shallow water
Water scorpions living in pond habitats

key_details: Multi-layer filtration removes suspended soil particles
Clear water may still harbor microscopic pathogens
Boiling destroys invisible disease-causing germs
real_world_examples: Cloth, sand, and gravel filter experiments

key_details: Preserving traditional water structures
Inspiring public water stewardship and innovation
real_world_examples: Jal Shakti Museum in New Delhi
